title: Trust calibration playbook for tiered inference degradations
content:
Purpose:

This playbook gives concise, GTM-focused guidance for communicating with customers when inference quality or capacity is partially impaired. It focuses on three practical outputs for go-to-market teams: (1) a taxonomy of fallback pathways we can surface as product guarantees, (2) short, composable customer-facing scripts for different channels and severity levels, and (3) competitive implications and positioning angles that preserve customer trust and commercial momentum.

Why this matters:

When inference availability or latency slips, customers evaluate two things quickly: whether the vendor is in control, and whether the vendor is candid about tradeoffs. Our goal is to make Redwood the vendor that customers trust to manage complexity — to communicate a clear escalation path, offer predictable alternatives, and show measurable guardrails. That trust reduces churn, shortens renewal conversations, and protects upsell motions.

Audience:

- Sales and account teams (deal preservation language, objections)
- Customer success and support (incident-first scripts, remediation commitments)
- Marketing & product comms (status page copy, release notes)
- Solutions engineers (technical fallback descriptions to feed customer plans)

Core positioning pillars (GTM framing):

1) Confidence through predictability — explain the planned fallback and what customers can expect (latency, model differences, cost).
2) Transparency without noise — honest, succinct statements that avoid technical overload for product teams but can link to details for platform engineers.
3) Control and options — present choices (fail-open to cheaper model, region failover, queued requests) and their user-visible tradeoffs.

Fallback taxonomy (how we describe options to customers):

- Model-tier fallback: automatic switch from primary model to a verified smaller model variant (e.g., from rdx-large to rdx-medium-quant). Messaging: "We can switch to a lower-latency, cost-efficient model that preserves intent but uses a smaller context/quality envelope."

- Region failover: route requests to an alternate region with compatible models. Messaging: "We’ll run your requests from a nearby region with identical policies — you may see +20–60ms latency depending on geography."

- Capacity tier fallback (graceful queuing): accept requests but add short queued windows with progress updates. Messaging: "We’ll queue bursts for up to X seconds and serve in order to preserve cost and response stability."

- Degraded feature mode: disable heavy features (e.g., long-context token streaming, tool-calling) temporarily. Messaging: "Certain advanced features (long-context streaming) will be temporarily limited to preserve overall throughput."

- Customer-configured safe-fallbacks: customer pins an allowed fallback option in their config (preferred for enterprise customers). Messaging: "You can pin an approved model and region as your guaranteed fallback; we will never route outside that config."

Example severity levels and recommended channel + tone:

- Level A: Partial latency increases (non-blocking). Channel: status page + in-app banner + automatic email for customers above commit threshold. Tone: factual, low friction.
  - Status page: "We’re seeing higher-than-normal token latency in us-west. We’re routing new requests to an alternate pool to maintain throughput; you may see brief increases in response times. Investigating."
  - Support snippet: "We’ve automatically routed traffic to an alternate pool. No action on your side needed — reach out if you see persistent errors."

- Level B: Regional capacity reduction affecting a subset of customers. Channel: targeted email, AM/SE outreach for impacted accounts. Tone: proactive, prescriptive.
  - Email subject: "Actionable update: temporary region capacity impact and your options"
  - Email body bullets: "What happened, who’s affected, safe temporary options (model-tier fallback, region failover), recommended next steps, ETA for remediation."

- Level C: Feature degradation or rollback (functional changes). Channel: support + AM + public incident update. Tone: accountable, commitment-focused.
  - Public incident update: "We experienced a degradation affecting X feature. We implemented an immediate rollback and are running a controlled rollout. If you need guaranteed behavior, configure the \"pin fallback\" setting in Console; our team can assist."

Composable messaging templates (short, re-usable):

- Short status banner (30–60 chars): "Partial capacity impact — some requests slower"

- Customer support opening line: "We’re aware of an issue affecting inference throughput. We’ve enabled an automated fallback that preserves responses while we remediate. Can I confirm whether you prefer region failover or pinned fallback?"

- Sales objection reply: "We build predictable fallbacks into our routing — during partial outages we surface options that keep your app functional and maintain service credits per the SLA. Happy to walk through a runbook tailored to your traffic profile."

- Exec-facing summary (for enterprise customers): "We detected transient capacity pressure in one cluster. Immediate mitigation: model-tier failover + region spill. Root cause under investigation; ETA for full restoration 6–12 hours. We’ll share a post-incident timeline and action plan within 48 hours."

Incident narrative templates (short examples to copy/paste):

- Minimal-impact narrative (for status page): "At 11:03 PST we observed higher token latency across a subset of nodes serving rdx-large. We routed traffic to a validated medium-size model and alternate pool; the majority of requests continued successfully. Ongoing monitoring; no customer data exposure."

- Escalated narrative (for targeted email): "On 2026-02-18 our telemetry showed sustained queuing across us-east pools due to an autoscaler regression. Mitigation: manual scale-up and cross-region spill; rollback of the autoscaler patch. We’re engaging SRE and the release team — expected full consistency restoration by 02/19. If you require formal assurance, we will propose a dedicated capacity carve-out."

Competitive implications and positioning guidance:

- Large cloud providers (managed endpoints): They often default to single-region SLA variability and opaque autoscaling. Our GTM angle: Redwood offers transparent fallback choices and per-route observability — not just an opaque endpoint. Emphasize visibility (token-level cost/latency) and ability to pin policies.

- Smaller LLM APIs (simplicity-first providers): Their promise is simplicity but they frequently lack multi-region failover or verified secondary models. Angle: simplicity is great — but for production apps, predictability matters. Highlight contractable fallback guarantees for enterprise customers.

- Self-hosted runtimes / inference vendors: They may promise full control but require significant ops lift. Angle: Redwood provides the same control surface (pinning, private deployment) while reducing operational burden with built-in fallbacks and SRE playbooks.

Operational checklist for GTM + SE handoff during an incident:

1) Identify impacted customer cohort (by model, region, SLA tier).
2) Determine recommended fallback(s) based on customer profile.
3) Draft an incident narrative using templates above and tailor SLAs/credits if required.
4) Notify AM/SE assigned to each impacted account with a 1–2 line action (e.g., "AM: offer pinned fallback; SE: confirm integration steps").
4) Publish status page + targeted comms.
5) Post-incident follow up: executive summary, ETA, and concrete remediation steps; schedule a retrospective with engineering input.

Tactical dos and don’ts for messaging:

- Do: use clear, customer-centric outcomes (what they see, how it affects users, how long it’ll take).
- Do: offer an explicit, low-friction remediation path (toggle, pin, rollback request form).
- Don’t: over-promise precise ETA if unknown; signal a window and commit to a follow-up time.
- Don’t: bury tradeoffs in technical jargon — give an option to read a technical appendix instead.

SLA & legal considerations (GTM-safe language):

- When quoting SLAs in sales collateral, avoid implying zero risk for multi-region events. Use phrasing like: "We maintain an availability SLA with graded credits; in some multi-region degradations, predefined fallback behavior will be initiated to maintain core functionality."
- For enterprise customers, add a line: "Pinning a dedicated capacity pool can be contracted for guaranteed throughput and isolation."

Examples of “pin fallback” GTM offers (commercial hooks):

- Silver fallback: automatic model-tier fallback with per-token parity guarantees for NPS-critical routes.
- Gold fallback: multi-region automatic failover + SRE-runbook + 4-hour remediation SLA for committed routes.
- Platinum: dedicated capacity pool with hot standby in an alternate region, quarterly runbook tests, and on-call support.

Measurement and KPIs to monitor messaging effectiveness:

- Time-to-first-communication (target < 30 min for committed accounts)
- Customer satisfaction post-incident (CSAT target > 85% for incidents)
- Number of at-risk renewals after incident (target: reduce churn compared to baseline)

Open questions for product/engineering (items to feed back):

- Can Console expose a one-click "pin fallback" that enforces region and model constraints?
- What are verified equivalent models (quality/latency) per model family to make product claims safe?
- Can we add templated runbooks per account (for high-commit customers) to reduce AM lift?

Next steps (GTM workstream):

1) Review this playbook with SRE and product to ensure claims match operational capabilities (owner: Asha; Due: 2026-03-01).
2) Create a short battlecard for sales with objection-handling scripts (owner: Jonah; Due: 2026-03-08).
3) Draft a status-page template and in-app banner variants (owner: Priya; Due: 2026-02-28).
4) Pilot the "pin fallback" messaging on 10 enterprise accounts and capture feedback (owner: Marco; Due: 2026-04-01).

Appendix: concise checklist for AM/SE outreach (copyable):

- Subject: "Update on inference behavior — recommended quick steps"
- Bullets: "1) We routed to an alternate model/region to keep traffic flowing. 2) If you prefer guaranteed behavior we recommend pinning a fallback (we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough). 3) We will follow up with a post-incident summary within 48 hours."

End of playbook.
